workflow: Read the open-call skill, taskbook, repository schemas, validators, and the user-provided planning reference before selecting a concept.
Translated the approved concept into a six-chapter planning argument, structured evidence registers, and a three-level spatial framework.
Derived provisional EPSG:4326 design layers, recomputed EPSG:4548 metrics, and cross-linked proposal claims to sources, assumptions, standards, geometry, and metrics.
Generated five figures, an offline report, an offline evidence dashboard, a 36-page A3 booklet, and six A0 boards from submission-local data.
Applied test-first checks, independent specification and quality reviews, PDF rendering inspection, browser inspection, and repository validators before final packaging.
tools: OpenStreetMap Overpass API snapshot with ODbL attribution
Shapely and pyproj for geometry and metric recomputation
Matplotlib and Pillow for evidence figures
ReportLab, pypdf, pdfplumber, and Poppler for PDF production and QA
HTML/CSS/JavaScript with Microsoft Edge DevTools Protocol for offline dashboard QA
data_flow: Public taskbook, repository standards, and user-provided public planning PDF -> sources.json and assumptions.json.
Provisional boundary plus frozen OSM background -> nine GeoJSON layers; OSM remains background-only and does not establish an official redline.
GeoJSON layers -> metrics.json through EPSG:4548 recomputation -> figures, proposal, HTML, booklet, and boards.
Proposal claims -> compliance_matrix.json, standard_matrix.json, and design_depth_matrix.json -> self-check and final manifest hashes.
human_inputs: The contributor identified the corridor from Beijing North Railway Station toward Jianting Bridge and named relevant universities, heritage sites, parks, and Zhongguancun innovation assets.
The contributor supplied P020200213595742434523.pdf, the publicly approved Haidian District Plan (2017-2035), for directional planning reference.

The contributor approved the strategic emphasis on implementability, risk and compliance, and AI-enabled planning innovation, and approved the six-chapter narrative structure and final execution direction.
reproducibility: External build scripts and frozen OSM payload are intentionally not part of the inert submission package; every public claim is independently inspectable through the committed JSON, GeoJSON, HTML, PNG, and PDF artifacts.
limitations: The competition redline and three key-area polygons were not supplied. All submitted boundaries are explicitly provisional, non-official, low-confidence geometry and must be replaced and recomputed when organizer polygons arrive.

The OSM snapshot covers only the stated bbox and is background-only; it cannot establish engineering positions, entrances, passenger flows, property rights, heritage controls, or statutory planning conditions.
Floor area, FAR, road area, and road ratio remain unknown because official parcel, building, road-width, and control-plan data are unavailable.

All projects, phases, thresholds, and AI services are concept-stage recommendations subject to professional survey, public participation, procurement, privacy impact assessment, safety review, and competent-authority approval.
No claim in this package represents government endorsement, statutory approval, a construction commitment, or an operational guarantee.
